interpretations.scope: Five completed evaluations, single shortened compliant geometry, terminal weight fixed at 0.05.
interpretations.statement: On the shortened compliant geometry at fixed terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.05, holding_max_speed is ~0.0127 m/s and passing for holding∈{0.0,0.05} but ~0.022-0.023 m/s and failing for holding∈{0.075,0.09,0.10}, with a non-monotone jump concentrated between 0.05 and 0.075.
interpretations.uncertainty: Five sparse points and no repeats; the boundary between 0.05 and 0.075 is unresolved and a discrete regime change cannot be excluded.

interpretations.scope: Observed plan behavior summary in the retained profiles.
interpretations.statement: The solver plan-selection signature (initialization_selected=13, accepted_noninitialization_plans=22) coincides with failing holding=0.075 and 0.09 but not with failing holding=0.10 (init=14, accepted=21), so plan selection does not cleanly account for all failing points.
interpretations.uncertainty: Counts are a coarse proxy for solver plan selection; no full future-plan replay is available.

interpretations.statement: Because every shortened-geometry trial held terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.05, the terminal-weight axis is unexplored there; a single terminal-weight perturbation at fixed failing holding is the affordable test separating a holding-dominated response from a holding×terminal interaction.
interpretations.uncertainty: Interaction magnitude is unknown; a null result at holding=0.09 would not exclude interaction near the 0.05 boundary.

fidelity_limits: Only the shortened compliant geometry is used; material scenario, section scale and topology are fixed.
Only two control/recipe weight paths are varied; no cross-terms beyond these two single-factor points.
Solver plan selection is read from profile counts, not from a full future-plan replay.
Numerical simulation only; acceptance implies neither real-time nor causal success.
plan.hypothesis: On the shortened compliant geometry, the holding_max_speed differences are dominated by a holding-weight response, possibly with discrete solver-plan-selection regime changes, rather than a narrow holding×terminal interaction; perturbing one weight at a time from the source (holding 0.09 / terminal 0.05) — a boundary point (holding 0.06 / terminal 0.05) and a terminal perturbation (holding 0.09 / terminal 0.10) — will show whether the outcome tracks holding weight, tracks terminal weight, or flips with plan-selection counts.
plan.rationale: All five shortened-compliant evaluations fixed terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.05, leaving the terminal axis and the 0.05-0.075 holding boundary untested. Anchoring two single-factor perturbations at the source (0.09/0.05) on the same frozen structure: candidate (0.06/0.05) probes holding-axis boundary/monotonicity; candidate (0.09/0.10) probes the terminal axis at fixed failing holding to test holding×terminal interaction. Structure is held fixed, so structural sensitivity is not varied within the batch, and control.profile_report records plan-selection behavior so a coincident regime change is visible. Two backend attempts stay within the per-batch cap and remaining budget.
stopping_conditions: Material or unknown backend failure on either candidate.
Both candidates reach a complete profiled evaluation.
weakening_observations: Candidate 1 (0.06/0.05) returns exactly the passing 0.05/0.05 metrics and candidate 2 (0.09/0.10) returns exactly the failing 0.09/0.05 metrics, i.e., both single-factor perturbations are inert and add only robustness.
The two runs differ in initialization_selected without any metric change, indicating plan-selection counts are not a reliable cause proxy.

arguments.reasoning: The five shortened-compliant evaluations all fixed terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.05, so the terminal-weight axis is untested on this geometry, and the only discriminating contrast available is on the holding axis. Holding_max_speed is low/passing at holding∈{0.0,0.05} and rises to ~0.022-0.023 m/s (failing) at holding∈{0.075,0.09,0.10}, with a non-monotone jump between 0.05 and 0.075. Solver plan-selection counts (initialization_selected 13 vs 14) match two of the three failures but not holding=0.10, so plan selection does not cleanly explain the pattern. Two single-factor perturbations of the source (0.09/0.05) on the same frozen structure best separate the competing causes: candidate 1 (0.06/0.05) probes the untested holding boundary/monotonicity, and candidate 2 (0.09/0.10) probes the untested terminal axis at fixed failing holding to test holding×terminal interaction. Keeping the structure fixed removes structural sensitivity as a within-batch cause, and the control.profile_report readout exposes whether any holding-speed change coincides with a plan-selection regime change. This uses two backend attempts, within the per-batch cap and remaining budget.
unresolved_uncertainties: Boundary and monotonicity of holding_max_speed between holding 0.05 and 0.075 on the shortened compliant geometry.
Whether observed plan-selection counts are reproducible or only coincidentally correlated with outcomes.
Whether a terminal-weight change can flip the holding-speed outcome (strength of holding×terminal interaction).
Whether the single passing configuration is robust across compliant/stiff material scenarios (structural sensitivity) rather than specific to the fitted weight.
Within-configuration variability is unknown because no configuration has been executed twice.
